newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees room for grain rebound if rain lasts.
newsitem.headline: France sees room for grain rebound if rain lasts.

text.p: France's farm ministry, reporting on grain harvests after months of drought, said on Wednesday the crops still had room for recovery if May brought ample rain.
A break in four months of dry weather in late April, followed by steady rain in the first week of May, helped but was not enough to protect yields in shallow soil areas, it said.
However last year's recovery from drought to record harvests could set a precedent if the rainfall remains extensive.
"Following last year's pattern which led to record crops, the impact on crops can be limited if there is ample rain in May," the ministry's SCEES statistics office said.
Wednesday brought erratic showers to much of the French grain area, a band stretching southwest from the Paris basin to the maize-growing southwest, weather office Meteo France said.
Fine weather dominated the north and west and high winds were reperted in the east and southeast.
Thursday would be cloudy and unstable in western and central France and warm in the east. Friday would be mostly sunny.
Longer range forecasts for late May were unavailable.
The farm ministry noted last year's record harvest of 62 million tonnes had been achieved after prolonged rain, not only in May but during the following months.
This had allowed the grain to ripen in excellent conditions.
However, except in the northeast of the country, the water deficit in early 1996 had been worse overall than this year.

Grain industry analysts have said some yield losses are inevitable in France this year, especially in the dry south. But a three percent overall rise in sowings could hold production reasonably steady as long as more rain arrived.
The ministry said that despite late rain in April 1997, rainfall for the month as a whole had been 60 percent below normal in the northern Paris grain basin.
The southeast received 85 percent less rain than usual.
The region least affected was the northeast which had a deficit if 43 percent.
